subject: SIG & SOC2: request for control provenance and dynamic access snapshot
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zenithbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@zenithbank.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: control provenance + dynamic access snapshot for SIG pack

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our vendor due diligence and the SIG questionnaire intake, our security team has a couple of follow-ups focused on control provenance and recent privileged-access activity. Specifically they asked for:

- A control provenance index (mapping of implemented controls to internal procedures, relevant logs, and evidence artifacts)
- A time-boxed dynamic access snapshot for the last 30 days (who had privileged access to the inference runtime and KMS keys, and any elevation events)
- Confirmation of which SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls are covered by your managed service vs customer responsibilities

Can you share the expected delivery timeline and the artifact formats you prefer? If you already have a SIG evidence pack or a pre-built mapping, that would be ideal.

Emily Zhang
Security Analyst, Vendor Risk Management
Zenith Bank

---
Attachment: initial-sig-ask-zenith.pdf (summary of requested fields)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zenithbank.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@zenithbank.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control provenance + dynamic access snapshot for SIG pack

Emily —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can assemble a SIG-ready evidence bundle that includes:

1) Control provenance index: PDF mapping with links to underlying artifacts and owner contact info.
2) Dynamic access snapshot: CSV export with privileged roles, user ids, start/end times, and elevation audit entries for the last 30 days.
3) Responsibility matrix: Single-page table showing which SOC2/ISO controls are "Redwood-managed" vs "Customer-managed" with short notes.

Proposed timeline:
- Draft artifacts (control index + snapshot) by Tue, 20 Apr EOD PT
- Finalized bundle (including SIG mapping spreadsheet) by Thu, 22 Apr EOD PT, subject to any follow-ups

I'll loop in Jordan and Karthik for the technical exports and mapping. Are CSV and PDFs OK for your intake system? Also confirm if you need signed attestations or just exported logs and certification references.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_evidence_readme.txt (instructions and file manifest)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zenithbank.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@zenithbank.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Request: control provenance + dynamic access snapshot for SIG pack

Looping infra and controls —

Quick technical notes on the exports we can provide (draft plan):

- Dynamic access snapshot: produce a CSV with columns [timestamp_utc, user_principal, internal_user_id, role, resource_type, resource_id, action, elevation_reason, session_id]. We can include both console and API-based elevation events.
- KMS key access: separate CSV with KMS key id, principal, operation, timestamp, region, request_id.
- Audit log retention: confirm logs are available for the requested 30-day window; full audit trail retained for 365 days per our policy (SOC2/ISO requirement).
- Control provenance index: generate a PDF that references code-level ownership (repo paths), runbooks (confluence links), and any signed attestations (SOC2 report excerpts).

Attachments (for draft delivery) attached: redwood_dynamic_access_snapshot_20270419.csv (sample), redwood_control_provenance_index.pdf (draft), sig_mapping_draft_zenith.xlsx (work-in-progress mapping of SIG questions to artifacts).

ETA: I’ll produce the CSV and KMS export by EOD today and hand off to Karthik for SIG mapping.

Jordan Blake
Senior SRE, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: redwood_dynamic_access_snapshot_20270419.csv, redwood_control_provenance_index.pdf, sig_mapping_draft_zenith.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zenithbank.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@zenithbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control provenance + dynamic access snapshot for SIG pack

Emily/Team —

Thanks — I’ve started the SIG crosswalk. A few highlights and clarifications that will help Zenith triage quickly:

- SOC 2: We will call out relevant CC criteria and map evidence. Example: CC6.1 (Logical access) → dynamic access snapshot + access control policy + periodic access review artifacts.
- ISO 27001: Annex A controls mapped where applicable (A.9 for access control, A.12 for operations).
- SIG: I’ve added a column in the spreadsheet for SIG question IDs and a confidence level (evidence present / partial / not applicable).

Outstanding clarifications needed from Zenith to finalize mapping:
1) Do you require user identifiers to be SSO email addresses, or can we supply hashed internal IDs plus a separate mapping file? (We can produce both, but hashed IDs are often preferred for PII minimization.)
2) Any objections to a redacted sample of elevation events (we can redact commands/arguments but keep metadata)?

Once we confirm those two points I’ll finalize the mapping and push the SIG workbook and provenance PDF to the shared Drive folder.

Planned delivery: control index + dynamic snapshot (finalized) by Tue, 20 Apr 2027 EOD PT; SIG workbook by Thu, 22 Apr.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Applied Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-EVIDENCE-zenith

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zenithbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@zenithbank.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control provenance + dynamic access snapshot for SIG pack

Vanessa / Karthik / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample attachments. CSV and PDF are fine; for identifiers we prefer hashed internal IDs plus a separate mapping file that lists the hash->email mapping delivered via a secure channel (email to our GRC inbox is fine). Redacted elevation events are acceptable provided metadata (timestamp, actor, reason) remains intact.

The proposed timeline works for Zenith. Please upload the finalized artifacts to the Drive link you provided and notify our GRC inbox when the mapping file is available. After our internal review we may have a couple of clarifying questions but this should get us past the initial SIG intake.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to the bundle.

Emily Zhang
Security Analyst, Vendor Risk Management
Zenith Bank
